title: Stable headroom scheduler and policy-layered admission for progressive degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a stable-headroom admission controller that combines an epochal token reservoir with policy layers (tenant quotas, SLO-aware priorities, temporal headroom) to enable predictable progressive degradation under multi-region load spikes and failover. This ticket covers design, prototype, and integration into the serving edge admission path.
background: We currently use lane-based admission with ad-hoc token buckets and multiple fallback modes. During multi-region failover tests we've observed bursty tenant amplification and oscillation of soft-degrade decisions. Operators need a mechanism that ensures: (1) bounded risk of SLA miss for high-SLO tenants, (2) fair long-term share across tenants, (3) graceful fidelity degradation modes rather than abrupt failures, and (4) fast recovery without oscillation when capacity returns.
proposal: Introduce a Stable Headroom Scheduler (SHS) that maintains short epochs (configurable 2s-10s windows) of reservation tokens per tenant computed from recent SLO burn rates, capacity headroom, and regional failover budgets. Admission decisions happen in policy layers: (A) Hard filters (auth, model-compatibility), (B) SLO-protect layer that reserves minimum tokens for high-SLO tenants, (C) Elastic fair-share layer that allocates remaining epoch tokens using a lightweight deficit round-robin weighted by configured tenant weight and recent consumption, (D) Degradation policy that, if admission denied, applies a progressive fallback (response trimming, compressive decoding, lower-redundancy model variant, or 204/429) selected by configured fidelity ladder. The controller should support per-route override and a global emergency cap for fleet-wide protective behavior.
implementation_notes:
- Add SHS module in runtime admission service with an in-memory epoch reservoir per shard. Epoch boundaries are aligned to 100ms ticks for smoother refill.
- Token computation: base_token = min(capacity_budget*epoch_length, tenant_commitment_rate*epoch_length). Adjust with burn_safety = max(1.0, 1 + recent_SLO_violation_rate*alpha).
- Persistent config: tenant_weight, min_reserved_tokens, fidelity_ladder (ordered list of fallbacks), regional_fallback_priority. Use existing config store (ConfigDB) with schema versioning.
- Metrics: expose per-tenant epoch_allocated, epoch_used, admission_denied_count, fallback_applied (label=fallback_type).
- API: admission API returns (allowed:bool, tokens_consumed:int, chosen_fallback:string|null, debug_trace:string). Debug trace included behind debug sampling flag to avoid overhead.
- Backpressure integration: upstream routers will interpret chosen_fallback to transform request or return early responses.
- Persistence note: only ephemeral per-epoch state kept in memory; no long-term persistence required.
- Failover: when region R fails, SHS increases headroom factor for surviving regions using configured failover_multiplier and migrates epoch budgets for moved tenants gradually over N epochs to avoid sudden bursts.
algorithms:
1) Epoch refill: every epoch E, for each tenant T compute reserved = clamp(min_reserved_tokens, weight_fraction * epoch_capacity, tenant_commit_rate*epoch_length * safety_factor).
2) Admission decision: if request.tokens <= tenant.epoch_available then allowed and decrement. Else consult degradation policy: attempt the next fallback in fidelity_ladder that fits token budget. If none, deny with 429.
3) Elastic fair-share: allocate remaining tokens after reserved tokens using deficit-rr: maintain deficit counter D_T += weight_T*quantum; choose tenants with D_T >= request_cost.
4) Oscillation damping: supply exponential moving average of epoch_available to avoid abrupt increases; apply hysteresis when toggling fallbacks (min_hold = 3 epochs).
metrics_and_slos: Primary observability goals: keep p99 latency under SLO for high-SLO tenants, control overall error-rate, prevent starvation. Key metrics: epoch_capacity_utilization, per-tenant_admit_rate, per-tenant_denied_rate, fallback_rate_by_type, oscillation_count (fallback toggles per tenant per minute), regional_headroom_factor. Dashboards: Global SHS health, Top 50 tenants by denied_rate, Fidelity ladder usage heatmap. Alert thresholds: >5% tenants with sustained denied_rate>0.5% for 5m => Pager; oscillation_count > 10/min for top tenant => SRE runbook.
monitoring_and_logging:
- Emit structured events to stdout with labels: tenant_id, route, shard, epoch_id, decision, fallback.
- Sampling: debug_trace only for 0.1% of decisions, full traces on explicit tenant debug flags.
- Integrate with Console traces: provide per-route annotation and link to SLO burn dashboard.
- Add synthetic litmus tests (local chaos) generating controlled bursts to validate headroom behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests: epoch refill logic, deficit round robin fairness invariants, hysteresis. Integration tests: local cluster with 3 shards, run ramp, steady-state, and recovery scenarios; assert no oscillation and fairness bounds (95th percentile long-run allocation within +/-15% of configured weights). Chaos tests: kill a region and validate staged migration of budgets across epochs with preserved per-tenant reserved minima. Load tests: synthetic tenants with mixed SLOs to ensure p99 latency for protected tenants remains within SLO under 60% capacity loss scenario.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-gated rollout in canary shard (1% traffic) for 72h with elevated telemetry. 2) Gradual expansion to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 days if no critical alerts. 3) Add opt-in tenant flags and default-off for public region initially. 4) Operator runbook: endpoint to set emergency cap and to drain epoch reservoirs. 5) Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window, run fairness and SLO regression reports.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: miscomputed tokens could starve tenants or over-allocate causing SLO misses. Mitigation: start with conservative safety_factor >1.5, enable canary and guard rails (global emergency cap). Risk: complexity causes operator confusion. Mitigation: provide clear Console UI slices and per-tenant explainability. Risk: oscillation of fallbacks. Mitigation: hysteresis and EMA smoothing.
dependencies_details: Depends on: ingress rate tagging change (ENG-902111) to surface per-request tenant weight; ConfigDB schema update (ENG-23145) to store fidelity ladders and min reservations; Console panels requirement (follow-up PR to Console team).
open_decisions: default fidelity ladder ordering for low-latency routes
acceptance_criteria: SHS module compiled and running behind feature flag in canary shard
Automated tests covering refill and fairness edge cases
Dashboards show correct metrics and no regression for protected tenants in canary load test
Runbook updated with operator controls and emergency cap endpoint
